goal: Compare cross-model, multi-model, and single-model approaches for agentic code review in 2026 and recommend the best approach with tradeoffs across cost, accuracy, bias mitigation, latency, and operational complexity.
background:
Three approaches to define and compare — (1) single-model: one model/agent reviews a diff end-to-end; (2) multi-model: multiple instances of the same model family invoked with different prompts/lenses (e.g., security, performance, tests, UX); (3) cross-model: different model families (e.g., Claude + Codex/GPT + Gemini) reviewing the same diff with a judge or synthesis pass.

Decision factors to weigh: false-positive rate and triage cost; blind-spot coverage and complementarity across families; same-family bias and judge convergence; escalation patterns (witness, dispute, independent); latency budget per PR; token/inference cost; infrastructure and orchestration complexity; integration with PR workflows (GitHub, GitLab); reproducibility and audit trail.

Cite 2025–2026 industry patterns where possible: Anthropic Claude Code reviewers, OpenAI/Codex review agents, Google Gemini Code Assist, GitHub Copilot review, and open-source orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, agent swarms). Discuss how multi-agent code review research (e.g., debate, jury, lens-based fanout) has matured.

Deliverable: rank the three approaches by use case (high-stakes PRs, routine diffs, security audits, refactors, greenfield). Surface when to combine approaches (e.g., single-model for fast feedback, cross-model on merge to main). Explicitly call out failure modes and antipatterns for each approach.
